nodes.name: Theorem 3.1: thm transduce laminar tree blablabla laminar set system $\rightarrow$ laminar tree
nodes.statement:
Let~$\Sigma$ be an extended vocabulary,
    including a unary set predicate name~$\ensuremath{\mathsf{SET}}\xspace$
    and not including the binary relational symbol~$\mathsf{ancestor}$.
    There exists a non-deterministic \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\operatorname{C}_{2}}\xspace{\!\!}\ensuremath{\operatorname{MSO}}\xspace}\xspace-transduction~$\tau$
    such that,
    for each laminar set system~$(U,\mathcal{S})$
    represented as the $\{\ensuremath{\mathsf{SET}}\xspace\}$-structure~$\mathbb{S}$
    and inducing the laminar tree~$T$ with ${L(T)=U}$,
    and for each $\Sigma$-structure~$\mathbb{A}$
    with~$\mathbb{S}\sqsubseteq\mathbb{A}$,
    $\tau(\mathbb{A})$ is non-empty
    and every output in~$\tau(\mathbb{A})$
    is equal to some $\{\mathsf{ancestor}\}$-structure $\mathbb{T}$ representing~$T$.

nodes.name: Theorem 4.2: thm transduce weakly-partitive tree blablabla weakly-partitive set system $\rightarrow$…
nodes.statement:
There exists a non-deterministic \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\operatorname{C}_{2}}\xspace{\!\!}\ensuremath{\operatorname{MSO}}\xspace}\xspace-transduction~$\tau$
    such that,
    for every weakly-partitive set system~$(U,\mathcal{S})$
    represented as the $\{\ensuremath{\mathsf{SET}}\xspace\}$-structure $\mathbb{S}$
    and inducing the weakly-partitive tree $(T,\lambda,<)$
    represented as the $\{\mathsf{ancestor},\ensuremath{\mathsf{degenerate}}\xspace,\mathsf{betweeness}\}$-structure $\mathbb{T}$,
    we have $\mathbb{T}\in\tau(\mathbb{S})$
    and every output in $\tau(\mathbb{S})$ is a weakly-partitive tree of $(U,\mathcal{S})$.

nodes.name: Theorem 4.4: thm transduce modular decomposition blablabla graph $\rightarrow$ modular decomposition
nodes.statement:
There exists a non-deterministic \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\operatorname{C}_{2}}\xspace{\!\!}\ensuremath{\operatorname{MSO}}\xspace}\xspace-transduction $\tau$
    such that for every directed graph $G$ represented as the $\{\ensuremath{\mathsf{edge}}\xspace\}$-structure $\mathbb{G}$,
    $\tau(\mathbb{G})$ is non-empty
    and every output in~$\tau(\mathbb{G})$ is equal to some $\{\mathsf{ancestor},\ensuremath{\textsf{m}\text-\mathsf{edge}}\xspace\}$-structure $\mathbb{M}$
    representing the enriched modular decomposition~$(T,F)$ of $G$.

nodes.name: Theorem 5.3: thm transduce weakly-bipartitive tree blablabla weakly-bipartitive set system…
nodes.statement:
There exists a non-deterministic \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\operatorname{C}_{2}}\xspace{\!\!}\ensuremath{\operatorname{MSO}}\xspace}\xspace-transduction~$\tau$
    such that,
    for every weakly-bipartitive bipartition system~$(U,\mathcal{B})$
    represented as the $\{\ensuremath{\mathsf{BIPART}}\xspace\}$-structure~$\mathbb{B}$,
    $\tau(\mathbb{B})$ is non-empty and every output in~$\tau(\mathbb{B})$
    is equal to some $\{\ensuremath{\mathsf{t}\text-\mathsf{edge}}\xspace,\ensuremath{\mathsf{degenerate}}\xspace,\mathsf{betweeness}\}$-structure~$\mathbb{T}$
    representing the weakly-bipartitive tree~$\left(T,\lambda,(<_t)_{t\in \lambda^{-1}(\ensuremath{\mathsf{linear}}\xspace)}\right)$ of~$(U,\mathcal{B})$.

nodes.name: Theorem 5.6: blablabla graph $\rightarrow$ split decomposition
nodes.statement:
There exists a non-deterministic \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\operatorname{C}_{2}}\xspace{\!\!}\ensuremath{\operatorname{MSO}}\xspace}\xspace-transduction $\tau$
    such that for any connected, directed graph $G$ represented as the $\{\ensuremath{\mathsf{edge}}\xspace\}$-structure $\mathbb{G}$;
    $\tau(\mathbb{G})$ is non-empty
    and every output in~$\tau(\mathbb{G})$ is equal to some $\{\ensuremath{\mathsf{t}\text-\mathsf{edge}}\xspace,\ensuremath{\mathsf{c}\text-\mathsf{edge}}\xspace\}$-structure $\mathbb{H}$
    representing the canonical split decomposition of $G$.

nodes.name: Corollary 4.6: thm transduce cotree blablabla cograph $\rightarrow$ cotree
nodes.statement:
There exists a non-deterministic \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\operatorname{C}_{2}}\xspace{\!\!}\ensuremath{\operatorname{MSO}}\xspace}\xspace-transduction~$\tau$
    such that, for each cograph~$G$ modeled by the $\{\ensuremath{\mathsf{edge}}\xspace\}$-structure~$\mathbb{G}$,
    $\tau(\mathbb{G})$ is non-empty
    and every output in~$\tau(\mathbb{G})$ is equal to some $\{\mathsf{ancestor},\ensuremath{\mathsf{series}}\xspace,\ensuremath{\varepsilon\text-\mathsf{ord}}\xspace\}$-structure~$\mathbb{C}$
    representing the cotree~$(T,\gamma,<)$ of~$G$.

nodes.name: Theorem 5.7, Theorem 5.9: graph $\rightarrow$ bi-join blabla decomposition
nodes.statement:
There exists a non-deterministic \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\operatorname{C}_{2}}\xspace{\!\!}\ensuremath{\operatorname{MSO}}\xspace}\xspace-transduction $\tau$
    such that for any connected graph $G$ represented as the $\{\ensuremath{\mathsf{edge}}\xspace\}$-structure $\mathbb{G}$,

    and every output in~$\tau(\mathbb{G})$
    is equal to some $\{\ensuremath{\mathsf{t}\text-\mathsf{edge}}\xspace,\ensuremath{\mathsf{c}\text-\mathsf{edge}}\xspace\}$-structure $\mathbb{H}$ representing the skeleton graph of $G$.
